name: Mud Green
lede: Mud Green is a dark, yellow-leaning olive named for wet earth, close enough to Brownish Green that the library files the two as near-duplicates.

sections.title: A landscape word
sections.body:
The ColorHub library classifies Mud Green as a nature-tier name, built on the landscape word *mud* the way [[midnight-purple|Midnight Purple]] and [[mustard-green|Mustard Green]] are built on *midnight* and *mustard* [1]. Its only recorded source is the xkcd 2010 crowd survey, so an earlier coining is undocumented [1]. At hex #606602 it measures lightness 41 and chroma 49 in LCH, a dark, muted yellow-green [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[spanish-bistre|Brownish Green]], only 3.2 CIEDE2000 units away and logged in the library as a near-duplicate crowd name [1][2]. [[drabolve|Greenish Brown]] sits 4.8 units off, read as yellower and duller, and [[army-green|Army Green]] 6.8 units off, greener and duller [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 72 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.3%, as photographed, rarer than roughly half the named colors here [3]. The earliest match is a 1438 painting by Robert Campin, 572 years before the name's own 2010 record, which only means an aged photograph can resemble this hue, not that the painter mixed mud, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 7 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.8 times the archive's overall rate, and inside a painting it most often plays an accent [3].
